source.title: ImbSAM: A Closer Look at Sharpness-Aware Minimization in Class-Imbalanced Recognition
source.authors: Yi-Xuan Zhou; Y. Qu; Xing Xu; Heng-Tao Shen

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present; some table and figure layout is flattened.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports its own results showing that SAM's generalization gains in class-imbalanced recognition vary by class-frequency group, and that its tail-class performance can be worse than the CE baseline.
record.gate_note: The study tests SAM on class-imbalanced recognition, not the claim versions' specified settings. The anomaly-detection results are omitted because they do not measure held-out natural-label classification error. ImbSAM results are not cataloged as evidence for the claim because ImbSAM is the study's proposed method.
record.test_reason: The study tests SAM and ImbSAM on class-imbalanced recognition, but none of V1–V8. In particular, Hessian eigenvalues and traces are not V7's magnitude-scaled perturbation measure, and no train–test gaps or ranking against norm and margin measures are reported. SAM versus momentum SGD also does not test V4's adaptive-optimizer comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors argue that class-agnostic SAM neglects tail-class overfitting and propose class-aware ImbSAM to target it, reporting improvements in long-tailed classification and semi-supervised anomaly detection. Their general improvement claim has exceptions, including reduced DevNet anomaly AUCPR at anomaly ratios below 0.1.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies SAM and class-aware ImbSAM on class-imbalanced recognition, not the interventions and settings in the listed claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported effect varies by dataset and class-frequency split; on CIFAR100-LT, SAM lowers Few-class accuracy relative to CE, while its results vary across ImageNet-LT and iNaturalist splits.

fits_no_version.finding: SAM's accuracy effects differ across class-frequency groups. On CIFAR100-LT, Many and Medium accuracy rise from 77.8 to 79.7 and 46.6 to 49.3, while Few accuracy falls from 13.5 to 12.4. Overall CE accuracy is unchanged by SAM on ImageNet-LT and iNaturalist.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Class-agnostic SAM can improve overall or head-class accuracy without improving tail-class accuracy in long-tailed image classification.

fits_no_version.finding: Reweighting tail losses by factors from 2 to 20 gives Few accuracy of 12.3–13.5, compared with CE's 13.5, while overall accuracy remains above CE.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing tail-class loss weights within SAM need not recover tail-class accuracy on CIFAR100-LT.

fits_no_version.finding: On Few classes, SAM lowers the maximum Hessian eigenvalue from 14673 to 6329 and trace from 169024 to 68252 despite lower held-out accuracy; ImbSAM lowers both statistics further.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Lower unscaled Hessian eigenvalue and trace need not coincide with higher tail-class held-out accuracy across these optimization methods.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision
record.problems: The results concern class-imbalanced datasets and class-split accuracy rather than the claim versions' specified settings. No uncertainty estimates are reported. Hessian measurements are figure-only and no train-test gap is given.
record.rows_left_out: Semi-supervised anomaly-detection AUC results are outside the natural-label classification claim. ImbSAM performance comparisons are the proposed method's own results and were excluded under the row rules.

untested.parts: Coexistence of random-label fitting capacity and natural-label generalization, including chance-level random-label test accuracy.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the roles of local connectivity, sparsity, and initialization.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, and optimizer switching.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that reduce those effects.
Dropout's effect on test error and its dependence on training-set size, dropout strength, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance versus train–test gaps at similarly low training loss, and ranking against norm and margin measures.
Test-accuracy effects of removing memorized examples versus removing equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The exclusion rests on different interventions and measures, not merely different datasets. States are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8; the reported accuracy differences remain valid descriptive findings. No missing results test a listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out accuracy on natural labels.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD or momentum SGD.
Large-batch versus small-batch training under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to train-test gaps.
